sources.entry: Calibre - E-book library manager that can view, convert, and catalog e-books in most of the major e-book formats and provides a built-in Web server for remote clients. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python/deb

summary.one_liner: calibre is a cross-platform e-book manager that views, converts, edits, and catalogs e-books and can sync with e-book reader devices.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes calibre as an e-book manager that can view, convert, edit, and catalog e-books in all major e-book formats. It can communicate with e-book reader devices and fetch metadata for books from the internet. It can also download newspapers and convert them into e-books. The README says it runs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. It also notes a built-in Web server for remote clients, per the awesome-selfhosted listing. The README itself mostly links to external pages for the manual, screenshots, development setup, and build instructions, and says bug reports go to Launchpad rather than GitHub.
use_cases: transfer books to an e-reader device
serve an e-book library to remote clients
how_to_run: See the User Manual for installation and usage instructions.
Development setup is described in the README's Development section (linked externally).
Build binaries and installers using the Build instructions linked from the README.
notable: Cross-platform desktop app for Linux, Windows, and macOS
Converts and edits e-books across most major formats
Fetches metadata from the internet and downloads news as e-books
Built-in Web server for remote access (per awesome-selfhosted listing)
caveats: Bug reports and feature requests go to Launchpad; GitHub is only for code hosting and pull requests
README content is mostly links to external documentation, so details are not fully stated inline
